```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)

# Change this to your local dev_raw.rds path if it isn't next to this file
dev_path <- "dev_raw.rds"
```

```{r load-and-clean, include=FALSE}
if (!exists("dev")) {
  dev_raw <- readRDS(dev_path)

  # Pull Grace's clean-function chunk verbatim so both files share one recoding
  rmd   <- readLines("project_part1_data_exp.Rmd")
  start <- grep("^```[{]r clean-function", rmd)
  end   <- which(grepl("^```[[:space:]]*$", rmd) & seq_along(rmd) > start)[1]
  chunk <- rmd[(start + 1):(end - 1)]
  chunk <- chunk[!startsWith(chunk, "dev <- clean_pums") & !startsWith(chunk, "glimpse")]
  eval(parse(text = chunk))

  dev <- clean_pums(dev_raw)
}

# Same education grouping as 5(b) and Section 6 (deterministic recode)
dev <- dev |>
  mutate(SCHL_grp = cut(as.numeric(SCHL),
                        breaks = c(0, 15, 17, 19, 20, 21, 22, 24),
                        labels = c("< HS", "HS / GED", "Some college", "Associate",
                                   "Bachelor", "Master", "Prof / PhD")))
```

## Numeric covariates: Pearson correlation matrix

```{r numeric-matrix}
dev |>
  select(WKHP, WKWN, JWMNP, AGEP) |>
  cor() |>
  round(2) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Redundant categorical pairs (by construction)

Cross-tabulating the categorical covariates shows several pairs where one
variable fully determines the other. These come from how the ACS defines the
variables, not from anything about veterans.

```{r redundant-pairs}
dev |> count(LANX, ENG)        # ENG is "N/A" exactly when the person speaks only English
dev |> count(DRATX, DRAT)      # DRAT is "N/A" exactly when DRATX = No
dev |> count(SEX, PAOC)        # PAOC is only asked of women
```

## Comparison 1: VA disability rating vs. ACS-reported disability

```{r drat-dis-table}
drat_dis <- dev |>
  count(DRAT, DIS) |>
  group_by(DRAT) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup()

drat_dis |>
  filter(DIS == "With a Disability") |>
  transmute(DRAT, n_total = round(n / (pct / 100)), pct_with_ACS_disability = pct) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

```{r drat-dis-plot, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 3}
drat_dis |>
  mutate(DRAT = fct_rev(DRAT)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = pct, y = DRAT, fill = DIS)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("With a Disability" = "#b2182b",
                               "Without a Disability" = "grey75")) +
  labs(x = "% of veterans in rating group", y = "VA service-connected rating (DRAT)",
       fill = "ACS disability (DIS)",
       title = "Most highly-rated veterans report no functional disability") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Why it matters for prediction: the two variables split earnings differently.

```{r drat-dis-earnings}
dev |>
  group_by(DRAT, DIS) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            median_earnings = median(PERNP_adj),
            pct_zero_earnings = 100 * mean(PERNP_adj == 0),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Comparison 2: education vs. having a VA rating

```{r schl-dratx}
dev |>
  count(SCHL_grp, DRATX) |>
  group_by(SCHL_grp) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  filter(DRATX == "Yes") |>
  transmute(SCHL_grp, n_total = sum(n / (pct / 100)), pct_with_VA_rating = pct) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
``
